description: Renovate proposes container image, Nextflow, data release, CI tool and pinned Python package updates; Dependabot keeps the GitHub Actions and the docs pip file (.github/dependabot.yml).
One PR per tool: no group rules. How a PR is checked and what to revalidate by hand: docs/updating.md.

The images live in versions.env. conf/containers.config and docs/versions.md are generated from it and hold the same strings, so the same dependency is matched in all of them and one PR updates every copy. If a PR touches only versions.env, the generated-file checks fail and name the command to run.
Container images. The strings match the same image in three files:
and docs/versions.md (the Variable, Image and Pinned version cells).
Each file has a tag form (an optional @sha256 after the tag is kept) and a digest-only form (image@sha256:...).
The image name stops at ':' and '@', so a digest line never becomes a package named '...@sha256'.

customManagers.description: Nextflow: NEXTFLOW_VERSION in versions.env, the setup-nextflow pins in the workflows and the NXF_VER install lines in the docs, all in one PR. The fake nextflow of the fake-docker suite and its test case read NEXTFLOW_VERSION from versions.env, so they hold no copy to match.
actionlint, downloaded by version in the lint workflow.
gitleaks, downloaded by version in the lint workflow.
ShellCheck, the version input of the action-shellcheck step in the lint workflow.
The Renovate CLI of the dry run: RENOVATE_VERSION in renovate-dry-run.yml and the command at the end of docs/updating.md, in one PR.
The Python the docs workflow builds the site with (python-version of setup-python in docs.yml), read as the python image's tags. The python rule below sends every update to the dependency dashboard.

IPD-IMGT/HLA release step 8 types against: HLA_DB_RELEASE in scripts/lib/common.sh. The IMGTHLA repository tags each release v<x.y.z>-alpha. setup.sh checks the new hla.dat against the md5 that release lists, and step 8 builds a new T1K index for it.
pgsc_calc, the release steps 25 and 26 run: PGSC_CALC_VERSION in versions.env and its copy in conf/containers.config, in one PR. Every update waits on the dependency dashboard (rule below).
The Python packages the screenshot script installs (playwright, pillow and, on macOS, pyobjc-framework-Vision), pinned with == in tests/demo/retake-screenshots.sh.
Aldy, the CYP2D6 caller docs/21-cyrius.md recommends: the version in its prose and in its pip install line, in one PR.

description: Biocontainer tags are <version>--<conda build hash>_<build number>. Docker versioning reads the part after '--' as a suffix that must stay the same, and the hash changes between versions, so most of these pins would never see a newer tag.
This versioning ignores the hash and orders by version, then build number. A tag in any other shape (an unsuffixed tag, a four-part version) is not a version here and is never proposed.
A Python build prefix (py312 in 3.9.5--py312h6e8b409_0) is kept: only tags for the same Python are proposed. A noarch tag (pyhdfd78af) has no such prefix.

packageRules.description: Ensembl VEP tags are release_<major>.<minor>, which docker versioning cannot read. A major (a new Ensembl release) waits for approval on the dependency dashboard: it needs the matching cache (VEP_CACHE_RELEASE in versions.env, about 26 GB) moved in the same PR.

PCGR/CPSR: every update waits for approval on the dependency dashboard, because each release reads its own reference bundle and VEP cache (PCGR_DATA_BUNDLE and PCGR_VEP_CACHE_RELEASE in versions.env). The image comes from ghcr.io/sigven/pcgr (Docker Hub's sigven/pcgr stops at 2.2.5); the image matcher reads ghcr.io like any other registry. allowedVersions keeps the release tags (x.y.z): ghcr also carries development builds (2.3.2.9006) and .singularity tags.

The python image, and the Python of the docs workflow, wait for approval on the dependency dashboard. Step 21 installs Cyrius into the image with wheels hash-locked for the image's Python (the header of scripts/cyrius-constraints.txt names it); a new minor or major needs them resolved again in the same PR. A patch of the same minor is safe to approve: the image test runs Cyrius on it.

Hold: pypgx stays at 0.26.0. 0.27.0 pulled pandas 3.0 and broke every gene while its smoke test still passed. Lift the hold when upstream releases the pandas fix (expected in 0.28.0) and a pypgx-bundle tag of the same version exists; PYPGX_BUNDLE_VERSION moves with it.
Hold: plink2 stays at 2.00a5.10, the only versioned tag pgscatalog/plink2 ships and the build pgsc_calc uses.

Hold: the pgsc_calc images (ghcr.io/pgscatalog/...) are the ones pgsc_calc's conf/modules.config names at PGSC_CALC_VERSION; they move only with that release, by hand, after reading that file again (docs/25-prs.md, Maintenance).

Hold: the minimap2+samtools image of the Nextflow alignment task (MINIMAP2_SAMTOOLS_IMAGE in versions.env). BioContainers tags it with a hash, not a version, so there is nothing to compare. It moves by hand with MINIMAP2_IMAGE and SAMTOOLS_IMAGE: request the new pair in BioContainers/multi-package-containers (combinations/hash.tsv), then pin the new tag. scripts/ci/check-images.sh fails while its versions comment and those two tags disagree, so a Renovate bump of either names this image in its failing check.
Legacy tools, no automated bumps: Manta, Strelka2, duphold, Octopus and GRIDSS are archived or quiet upstream. Bump one by hand after running it on the fixture.

description: Step 26b's three tools, no automated bumps: their tags are not versions this versioning can read, so a lookup would only report them as invalid.

ADMIXTURE is tagged 1.3.0--0, without the conda hash and build number the biocontainers rule above needs, and 1.3.0 is the only build BioContainers publishes. RFMix is 2.03.r0.9505bfa--h503566f_8, a version with a commit in it, and 2.03 (2017) is its last release. Beagle is 5.5_27Feb25.75f--hdfd78af_0, whose real version is the date.
Bump one by hand after running step 26b on the e2e fixture; the monthly freshness issue reports a newer tag.

packageRules.description: Nextflow: every update waits for approval on the dependency dashboard. A new release can change what the strict config parser accepts, and the validated version is also written in nextflow.config and the Nextflow docs, which need reading by hand.

pgsc_calc: every update waits for approval on the dependency dashboard. PGSC_CALC_SHA256, PGSC_CALC_NF_SCHEMA and the PGSC_*_IMAGE lines (PGSC_PANEL too on a new release line) move with the release, by hand, after reading its nextflow.config and conf/modules.config again (docs/25-prs.md, Maintenance).
CI tools take the ci prefix: actionlint, gitleaks, ShellCheck and the Renovate CLI of the dry run.
